verdict.rationale: Host-side virtual displays for covered windows or headless machines are a fair question for a remote-desktop product like AnyDesk, so the axis applies. Nothing in the evidence pack mentions a virtual display, a headless display adapter, or rendering while covered. The CLI and REST API docs cover only installation, licensing, session management and account data.

support.subject: As a power user, the host can create a virtual display, so a streamed window keeps rendering when covered or the machine runs headless
